ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AD is the median of $\triangle ABC$, E is a point on AD, and BE intersects AC at F. If $BE=AC$, $BF=9$, and $CF=6$, then what is the length of $AF$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend AD to G such that DG = AD, and connect BG,\\
$\because$ AD is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ CD = BD,\\
In $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle GBD$,\\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}CD=BD \\ \angle ADC= \angle BDG \\ AD=DG \end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD \cong \triangle GBD$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAD = \angle G$, AC = BG,\\
$\because$ BE = AC,\\
$\therefore$ BE = BG,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle G = \angle BEG$,\\
$\because$ $\angle BEG = \angle AEF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEF = \angle EAF$.\\
$\therefore$ EF = AF,\\
$\therefore$ AF + CF = BF - AF,\\
i.e., AF + 6 = 9 - AF,\\
$\therefore$ AF = $\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and A is above; D is located on the base BC, and segment AD connects from A to the base D; E is located on AD; the straight line starting from B passes through E and then continues to intersect AC at F. It can be seen in the figure that B, E, F are collinear and the order is B-E-F, and A, F, C are collinear and F is on AC. Reasoning: Because AD is the median of triangle ABC, D is the midpoint of BC, that is, BD = DC. According to the auxiliary-line method, extend AD through D to G, making DG = AD, and connect BG. At this time D is simultaneously the midpoint of BC and AG. In triangle ACD and triangle GBD, DC = DB, AD = DG, and ∠ADC and ∠GDB are vertical angles, so the two triangles are congruent by SAS. Therefore AC = BG, and the corresponding angles ∠CAD = ∠BGD. Since E, D, G, A are on the same straight line, ∠BGD = ∠BGE, hence ∠CAD = ∠BGE. The problem states BE = AC, and from congruence AC = BG, so BE = BG. Thus triangle BEG is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, that is, ∠BGE = ∠BEG. Also because B, E, F are collinear, and A, E, G are collinear, ∠BEG and ∠AEF are vertical angles and are equal; at the same time A, F, C are collinear, and A, E, D are collinear, so ∠CAD = ∠EAF. Combining the above equal angles gives ∠AEF = ∠EAF, therefore in triangle AEF, EF = AF. Let AF = x. Because F is on AC and CF = 6, AC = AF + CF = x + 6. Also BE = AC, so BE = x + 6. In the figure B-E-F are collinear and E is between B and F, so BF = BE + EF = (x + 6) + x. It is known that BF = 9, therefore 2x + 6 = 9, solving gives x = 3/2. Therefore AF = 3/2.

method.method_draft: Auxiliary congruent-triangle route. First read the diagram: A is above base BC, D lies on BC, AD is drawn, E lies on AD, and the line through B and E continues to meet AC at F, with the order B-E-F on that line and A-F-C on AC. From the text use that AD is a median, so BD = DC, and use BE = AC, BF = 9, CF = 6. Extend AD past D to a point G so that DG = AD, then connect BG. Since D is the midpoint of BC and also of AG, triangles ACD and GBD are congruent by SAS, giving AC = BG and angle CAD = angle BGE. Because BE = AC, get BE = BG, so triangle BEG is isosceles and angle BGE = angle BEG. Since E lies on AD and B,E,F are collinear, angle BEG equals angle AEF; since A,D,E are collinear, angle CAD equals angle EAF. Therefore angle AEF = angle EAF, so EF = AF. Let AF = x. Then AC = x + CF = x + 6, and BE = x + 6. From the diagram order B-E-F, BF = BE + EF = (x + 6) + x = 9, so 2x + 6 = 9 and x = 3/2.

method.method_draft: Mass-points or barycentric-ratio route. First read the diagram: F lies on side AC, line BF passes through E, and E lies on the median AD; also the order is A-F-C on AC and B-E-F on the extended line through BE. Let AF = x, so from CF = 6, AC = x + 6. By BE = AC, BE = x + 6. Now use a mass-points setup in triangle ABC. Since F divides AC with AF:FC = x:6, assign endpoint masses m_A = 6 and m_C = x. Since AD is a median, D is the midpoint of BC, so the masses at B and C must be equal; hence m_B = m_C = x. The mass at F is m_A + m_C = x + 6. On line BF, the balancing point E satisfies BE:EF = m_F:m_B = (x + 6):x, so EF = x when BE = x + 6. Therefore BF = BE + EF = (x + 6) + x = 9. Solve 2x + 6 = 9 to get AF = x = 3/2.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是三角形 ABC，A 在上方，B 在左下，C 在右下。D 在底边 BC 上，线段 AD 从 A 连到 D；E 位于 AD 上。点 F 位于边 AC 上，并且从 B 出发的直线经过 E 后到达 F，所以顺序为 B-E-F；在边 AC 上顺序为 A-F-C。

推理：设 AF = x。因为 CF = 6，所以 AC = AF + CF = x + 6。又已知 BE = AC，因此 BE = x + 6。

用质量点法。F 在 AC 上，且 AF:FC = x:6，所以可取端点质量 m_A = 6，m_C = x。由于 AD 是三角形 ABC 的中线，D 是 BC 的中点，因此 B、C 两端质量相等，即 m_B = m_C = x。

于是 F 点的质量为 m_F = m_A + m_C = 6 + x。在线段 BF 上，E 为由这些质量确定的交点，所以 BE:EF = m_F:m_B = (x+6):x。又 BE = x+6，因此 EF = x。

因为图中 B-E-F 共线且 E 在 B 与 F 之间，所以 BF = BE + EF = (x+6) + x。已知 BF = 9，因此 2x + 6 = 9，解得 x = 3/2。故 AF = 3/2。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, AD is the median of $\triangle ABC$, E is a point on AD, and BE intersects AC at F. If $BE=AC$, $BF=9$, and $CF=6$, then what is the length of $AF$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend AD to G such that DG = AD, and connect BG,\\
$\because$ AD is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore$ CD = BD,\\
In $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle GBD$,\\
$ \left\{\begin{array}{l}CD=BD \\ \angle ADC= \angle BDG \\ AD=DG \end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD \cong \triangle GBD$ (SAS),\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAD = \angle G$, AC = BG,\\
$\because$ BE = AC,\\
$\therefore$ BE = BG,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle G = \angle BEG$,\\
$\because$ $\angle BEG = \angle AEF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEF = \angle EAF$.\\
$\therefore$ EF = AF,\\
$\therefore$ AF + CF = BF - AF,\\
i.e., AF + 6 = 9 - AF,\\
$\therefore$ AF = $\boxed{\frac{3}{2}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and A is above; D is located on the base BC, and segment AD connects from A to the base D; E is located on AD; the straight line starting from B passes through E and then continues to intersect AC at F. It can be seen in the figure that B, E, F are collinear and the order is B-E-F, and A, F, C are collinear and F is on AC.

Reasoning: Because AD is the median of triangle ABC, D is the midpoint of BC, that is, BD = DC. According to the auxiliary-line method, extend AD through D to G, making DG = AD, and connect BG. At this time D is simultaneously the midpoint of BC and AG. In triangle ACD and triangle GBD, DC = DB, AD = DG, and ∠ADC and ∠GDB are vertical angles, so the two triangles are congruent by SAS. Therefore AC = BG, and the corresponding angles ∠CAD = ∠BGD. Since E, D, G, A are on the same straight line, ∠BGD = ∠BGE, hence ∠CAD = ∠BGE.

The problem states BE = AC, and from congruence AC = BG, so BE = BG. Thus triangle BEG is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles are equal, that is, ∠BGE = ∠BEG. Also because B, E, F are collinear, and A, E, G are collinear, ∠BEG and ∠AEF are vertical angles and are equal; at the same time A, F, C are collinear, and A, E, D are collinear, so ∠CAD = ∠EAF. Combining the above equal angles gives ∠AEF = ∠EAF, therefore in triangle AEF, EF = AF.

Let AF = x. Because F is on AC and CF = 6, AC = AF + CF = x + 6. Also BE = AC, so BE = x + 6. In the figure B-E-F are collinear and E is between B and F, so BF = BE + EF = (x + 6) + x. It is known that BF = 9, therefore 2x + 6 = 9, solving gives x = 3/2. Therefore AF = 3/2.
